config.title: PropTypes / TypeScript Interface

intro.title: PropTypes / TypeScript Interface
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a simple Angular component that displays user profile information, such as a name and age. You will learn how to define and use a TypeScript interface to strictly type the data your component receives, ensuring it matches the expected structure. This involves creating an interface, applying it to a component's input property, and using the typed data in your template. By the end, you'll understand how interfaces help catch errors early and make your Angular code more reliable and maintainable.
intro.usecase: TypeScript interfaces are essential for building maintainable enterprise applications like customer dashboards and admin panels. In a dashboard component, interfaces define the structure of data objects like user profiles, sales metrics, or inventory items, ensuring type safety across complex data flows. When creating reusable form components or data tables, interfaces specify the expected props for inputs, validation rules, and event handlers. This prevents runtime errors in production applications and enables better IDE support during development of features like dynamic filters or interactive charts.

objectives: Define a TypeScript interface to describe the shape of component input data
Apply the interface to a component class by implementing it in the component's properties
Initialize component state with data that conforms to the defined interface
Bind interface-typed properties to template elements using Angular's data binding syntax
Manipulate component methods to handle and transform data according to interface constraints
Render dynamic content in the template by accessing properties defined in the interface
Update component inputs with new data while maintaining type safety through the interface

steps.title: Create a TypeScript interface for User data
steps.instruction: Below the imports, create a TypeScript interface named 'User' with three properties: 'id' of type number, 'name' of type string, and 'email' of type string.
steps.hint: Use the 'interface' keyword followed by the interface name and property definitions with type annotations.
steps.expectedOutcome: A TypeScript interface named 'User' with correctly typed properties will be defined.
successCriteria: The User interface is defined with id: number, name: string, and email: string properties.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but check that all three properties (id, name, email) have the correct types (number, string, string).
steps.feedbackWrong: The interface definition is missing or incorrect. Make sure to use the 'interface' keyword and include all three properties with their types.

steps.expectedOutcome: A UserProfile component class is created with proper Angular structure.
successCriteria: Component class is named UserProfile, uses @Component decorator, and implements OnInit interface.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.

steps.title: Define a user property with User interface type
steps.instruction: Inside the UserProfileComponent class, add a public property named 'user' with the type 'User' (the interface you created earlier).
steps.hint: Remember to use TypeScript type annotation syntax: propertyName: Type. Since this is a class property, you can declare it directly inside the class body.

steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.

steps.hint: Angular templates use double curly braces {{ }} to display component property values. Access the user property's name field.

{{ product.title }}

steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
